criteria.text: Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then every tab is reachable and every card drills down one level.
Given sample mode, when any tab is shown, then the sample data is visibly labelled as sample.

Given the Command Center, when any tab renders, then .colaberry/plan.json and .colaberry/progress.json are both committed in this repo and every tab reads its content from them at runtime rather than from hard-coded values.
Given the Command Center, when any tab is shown, then .colaberry/manifest.json is committed in this repo and every tab shows how old that data is and warns when the age exceeds a week.
Trust — no tab shows a number, a connection or a result the project has not actually produced.

stories.notes: Nine tabs, hash routes, sample/real switch. Agents tab uses story owners (plan has no agent roster). Data model is a proposal awaiting review. Run tests: node --test tests/command-center.test.mjs

criteria.text: Given a supported platform is in use, when a meeting starts, then the system detects it and begins audio capture.
Given a meeting ends, when the system detects this, then it stops capturing audio.
Trust: When audio capture starts, an entry is logged indicating the meeting start and consent verification.
Given the user has enabled auto-start, when the laptop boots, then the application starts automatically and runs in the system tray.
Given the application is running, when the user checks the system tray, then the application is visible there.
Trust: When the application starts, an entry is logged indicating the startup mode (manual/automatic).
Given a meeting is detected, when it starts, then the user receives a notification about the detection.
Given a transcript is ready, when the processing completes, then the user receives a notification about the transcript availability.
Trust: When a notification is sent, an entry is logged with the notification type and timestamp.
Given audio capture is active, when the user checks the application, then a clear indicator is visible.
Given transcription is active, when the user checks the application, then a clear indicator is visible.
Trust: When the indicator changes state, an entry is logged with the current state and timestamp.
Given the user accesses the settings, when they view data processing information, then the system clearly distinguishes between local and external data processing.
Given the user reviews the data policy, when they check the application documentation, then it accurately reflects data processing practices.
Trust: When data processing settings are updated, an entry is logged with the changes and timestamp.
Given a live meeting is in progress, when the system captures audio, then it generates a real-time transcript with speaker identification and timestamps.
Given overlapping conversations occur, when the system processes the audio, then it maintains the chronological order and identifies speakers correctly.
Trust: Given a meeting is transcribed, when the transcript is saved, then it includes timestamps and speaker identification for audit purposes.
Given a transcript with errors, when a user selects an audio segment, then they can replay the audio and correct the transcript.
Given a corrected transcript, when the user saves changes, then the updated transcript is stored with the corrections.
Trust: Given a correction is made, when the transcript is saved, then the system logs the correction for audit purposes.
Given a meeting has ended, when real-time transcription was unavailable, then the system generates the transcript immediately.
Given a generated transcript, when the user accesses it, then it is available in the meeting history.
Trust: Given a transcript is generated post-meeting, when it is saved, then it includes timestamps and speaker identification for audit purposes.
Given a transcript is saved, when it is stored, then it is encrypted using the specified encryption protocol.
Given an audio recording is saved, when it is stored, then it is encrypted using the specified encryption protocol.
Trust: Given encrypted data, when accessed, then it requires decryption keys for access.
Given a network interruption occurs, when the connection is restored, then transcription resumes from the last saved point.
Given an application crash occurs, when the application restarts, then transcription resumes from the last saved point.
Trust: Given a recovery event, when transcription resumes, then the system logs the event for audit purposes.
Given a user with multiple audio devices connected, when the system starts, then it must identify all available audio input and output devices.
Given a user switches from a built-in microphone to a Bluetooth headset during a meeting, when the system detects the change, then it must continue capturing audio without interruption.
Trust: The system logs all detected audio devices and any changes in device usage.
Given a meeting with background noise, when the system captures audio, then it must apply noise reduction to enhance clarity.
Given a user enables audio enhancement settings, when the system processes audio, then it must enhance the audio quality according to the settings.
Trust: The system logs the application of noise reduction and enhancement settings for each audio capture session.
Given a user accesses audio settings, when they adjust quality settings, then the system must apply these settings to subsequent audio captures.
Given a user sets a high-quality audio setting, when a meeting is recorded, then the audio must reflect the high-quality setting.
Trust: The system logs all changes to audio quality settings and their application to audio captures.
Given a user changes their audio configuration, when the system detects the change, then it must adapt without requiring a restart.
Given a user connects a new audio device mid-meeting, when the system detects the device, then it must switch to the new device seamlessly.
Trust: The system logs all configuration changes and adaptations made during audio capture.
Given a user on Windows, when the system captures audio, then it must comply with Windows-specific restrictions.
Given a user on macOS, when the system captures audio, then it must comply with macOS-specific restrictions.
Trust: The system logs compliance with OS-specific restrictions for each audio capture session.
Given multiple audio sources are used, when the system captures audio, then it must synchronize the inputs to prevent misalignment.
Given a user reviews a synchronized recording, when they play it back, then the audio must be coherent and aligned.
Trust: The system logs synchronization status and any adjustments made during audio capture.
Given a user selects an audio format, when the system captures audio, then it must save the recording in the chosen format.
Given a user changes the audio format setting, when a new recording is made, then it must reflect the new format.
Trust: The system logs the selected audio format for each recording session.
Given the user is logged in, when they access the dashboard, then they should see sections for ongoing, recent, and historical meetings.
Given a meeting is ongoing, when the user views the dashboard, then the meeting should appear under the ongoing section with its details.
Trust: Given the user accesses the dashboard, then the system must log the access time and user ID for audit purposes.
Given meetings are organized into projects, when the user searches by project, then only meetings from that project should be displayed.
Given the user searches by date, topic, participant, or keyword, when results are returned, then they should match the search criteria.
Trust: Given a search is performed, then the system must log the search criteria and user ID for audit purposes.
Given a user wants to delete a meeting, when they confirm the deletion, then the meeting and its recordings should be permanently removed.
Given a user wants to export their data, when they choose the export option, then they should receive their data in a downloadable format.
Trust: Given a data deletion or export action, then the system must log the action and user ID for audit purposes.
Given a user wants to download a transcript, when they select a format, then the transcript should be available in TXT, PDF, or DOCX format.
Given a user selects an unsupported format, when they attempt to download, then the system should display an error message.
Trust: Given a transcript download, then the system must log the download action and user ID for audit purposes.
Given a user selects local processing, when a meeting is processed, then it should be handled locally without cloud interaction.
Given a user selects cloud processing, when a meeting is processed, then it should utilize cloud resources.
Trust: Given a processing option is selected, then the system must log the selection and user ID for audit purposes.
Given a completed meeting, when the meeting ends, then the system generates a summary including key discussion points, decisions, and action items.
Given a completed meeting, when the system generates a summary, then the summary is saved automatically.
Trust: Given a generated summary, when it is saved, then it is logged with a timestamp and meeting ID.
Given a meeting type selection, when a user selects a format, then the system generates a summary in the chosen format.
Given an unsupported meeting type, when a user selects a format, then the system provides a default summary format.
Trust: Given a format selection, when a summary is generated, then the format choice is logged with the meeting ID.
Given a completed meeting without real-time transcription, when the meeting ends, then the system processes and generates a transcript.
Given an ongoing transcription, when the system is interrupted, then it automatically saves the transcription progress.
Trust: Given a transcription process, when it completes, then it is logged with a timestamp and meeting ID.
Given a completed meeting, when the system processes the transcript, then it generates a title based on discussion topics.
Given a meeting with no clear topics, when the system generates a title, then it uses a default naming convention.
Trust: Given a generated title, when it is saved, then it is logged with the meeting ID.
Given multiple meetings within a project, when summaries are generated, then the system consolidates them into a project-level summary.
Given a project with no meetings, when a summary is requested, then the system indicates no data available.
Trust: Given a project-level summary, when it is generated, then it is logged with a project ID.
Given a completed meeting, when the system processes the transcript, then it categorizes the meeting based on content.
Given a meeting with ambiguous content, when categorization is attempted, then the system uses a default category.
Trust: Given a categorized meeting, when it is saved, then the category is logged with the meeting ID.
Given an API key, when it is stored, then it is encrypted using industry-standard encryption.
Given a request for an API key, when it is retrieved, then it is decrypted securely.
Trust: Given an API key operation, when it is performed, then it is logged with a timestamp and operation type.
Given a transcript with uncertain segments, when the system detects low confidence, then it flags the segment for review.
Given a flagged segment, when the user reviews it, then they can see a confidence indicator.
Trust: Given a flagged segment, when the user corrects it, then the correction is logged in the audit trail.
Given an audio input, when the language is spoken, then the system automatically detects the language.
Given a multilingual conversation, when different languages are spoken, then the system identifies each language correctly.
Trust: Given a detected language, when the transcript is generated, then the language detection is logged.
Given a multilingual conversation, when the system transcribes, then it accurately transcribes each language spoken.
Given a conversation in multiple languages, when the user reviews the transcript, then each language is correctly identified and transcribed.
Trust: Given a multilingual transcript, when reviewed, then language transitions are logged.
Given a conversation with technical terms, when transcribed, then the system accurately recognizes and transcribes the terms.
Given a conversation with industry-specific vocabulary, when transcribed, then the system accurately recognizes and transcribes the vocabulary.
Trust: Given a transcript with technical terms, when reviewed, then recognized terms are logged.
Given an existing transcript, when the user requests regeneration, then the system regenerates the transcript.
Given a transcript with errors, when the user requests improvement, then the system improves the transcript.
Trust: Given a regenerated transcript, when reviewed, then changes are logged.
Given a transcript, when generated, then it is formatted with clear speaker identification and timestamps.
Given a transcript, when reviewed, then it is structured with paragraphs and punctuation.
Trust: Given a structured transcript, when reviewed, then formatting changes are logged.
Given an audio file, when processed offline, then the system transcribes it without internet access.
Given a lack of internet connection, when transcription is requested, then the system processes the audio offline.
Trust: Given an offline transcription, when completed, then the process is logged.
Given a completed transcription, when the user chooses to retain audio, then the audio is stored.
Given a completed transcription, when the user chooses to delete audio, then the audio is deleted.
Trust: Given a user choice on audio retention, when executed, then the action is logged.
Given a series of meetings with overlapping participants and topics, when the system processes these meetings, then it should identify them as related.
Given a meeting with no similar topics or participants, when processed, then it should not be marked as related to others.
Trust: The system logs the criteria used to determine meeting relationships.
Given a meeting transcript with project references, when processed, then the system should link it to the appropriate project.
Given a meeting transcript without project references, when processed, then it should not be linked to any project.
Trust: The system logs the project linkage decisions and criteria.
Given a series of meetings with decisions made, when processed, then the system should track these decisions across meetings.
Given a meeting with no decisions, when processed, then it should not add any decision tracking entries.
Trust: The system logs decision tracking entries and their sources.
Given a meeting where a previously agreed plan is changed, when processed, then the system should identify and log the change.
Given a meeting with no changes to plans, when processed, then it should not log any changes.
Trust: The system logs changes with references to the original agreements.
Given a recurring action item discussed in multiple meetings, when processed, then the system should track its recurrence.
Given a non-recurring action item, when processed, then it should not be tracked as recurring.
Trust: The system logs recurrence patterns and action item status.
Given unresolved issues discussed in multiple meetings, when processed, then the system should highlight these issues.
Given resolved issues, when processed, then they should not be highlighted as unresolved.
Trust: The system logs unresolved issues with references to meetings where they were discussed.
Given tasks discussed in meetings, when processed, then the system should identify their completion status.
Given tasks not discussed, when processed, then they should not have their status updated.
Trust: The system logs task status changes with references to relevant discussions.
Given a deadline mentioned in a meeting, when processed, then the system should remind the user about it before the due date.
Given no deadlines mentioned, when processed, then no reminders should be sent.
Trust: The system logs reminders sent and their corresponding deadlines.
Given a meeting is detected, when I manually start transcription, then the system begins transcribing the meeting.
Given transcription is ongoing, when I pause transcription, then the system stops transcribing until resumed.
Trust: Given transcription is paused, when I resume transcription, then the system continues transcribing from where it left off.
Given a question about a past meeting, when I ask the AI assistant, then it provides a contextual answer with references to the original meeting.
Given a question about a past meeting, when the AI assistant cannot find relevant information, then it informs the user that no data is available.
Trust: Given an AI-generated answer, when I view the references, then they include speaker names and timestamps.
Given an AI-generated answer, when the answer includes interpretations, then the system clearly labels them as interpretations.
Given an AI-generated answer, when the answer is based solely on discussed information, then the system does not label it as an interpretation.
Trust: Given a mixed answer, when I view the details, then the system distinguishes between discussed facts and interpretations.
Given the system settings, when I select local processing, then the system processes AI tasks locally.
Given the system settings, when I select cloud processing, then the system processes AI tasks in the cloud.
Trust: Given a processing mode change, when I view the system status, then it reflects the current processing mode.
Given related meetings, when I view a project, then the system shows a consolidated history of discussions and decisions.
Given a project history, when a new related meeting occurs, then the system updates the history with new discussions and decisions.
Trust: Given a project history, when I view it, then it accurately reflects all related meetings and decisions.
Given the application settings, When I exclude an application from detection, Then the system does not detect meetings from that application.
Given the application settings, When I attempt to exclude an unsupported application, Then the system notifies me that exclusion is not possible.
Trust: Given an excluded application, When a meeting starts, Then the system logs that the application was excluded from detection.
Given a completed meeting summary, When I choose to export it, Then the system exports to Google Calendar and other selected applications.
Given a completed meeting summary, When I attempt to export to an unsupported application, Then the system notifies me of the limitation.
Trust: Given an export action, When it completes, Then the system logs the export details including destination and timestamp.
Given system audio activity, When a meeting starts, Then the system detects and begins transcription.
Given microphone usage, When no meeting is detected, Then the system does not start transcription.
Trust: Given an active communication detection, When it occurs, Then the system logs the detection event with audio synchronization details.
Given the notification settings, When I configure preferences, Then the system updates my notification settings accordingly.
Given the notification settings, When I disable all notifications, Then the system does not send any alerts.
Trust: Given a notification configuration change, When it is saved, Then the system logs the change with a timestamp.
Given the integration settings, When I select applications for integration, Then the system connects to the chosen applications.
Given the integration settings, When I deselect an application, Then the system disconnects from that application.
Trust: Given an integration change, When it is saved, Then the system logs the change with application details.
Given the current architecture, When new features are added, Then the system scales without performance degradation.
Given the current architecture, When additional operating systems are supported, Then the system adapts without major changes.
Trust: Given a scalability test, When it is completed, Then the system logs performance metrics and scalability results.
Given the system is idle, When I check the resource usage, Then CPU and memory consumption should be minimal.
Given the system is idle, When I check the battery usage, Then the battery consumption should be efficient.
Trust: Given the system is idle, When I review the audit logs, Then no unnecessary processes should be running.
Given a meeting lasts several hours, When the meeting is processed, Then the system should handle it without data loss.
Given a long meeting is processed, When I check the transcript, Then it should be complete and accurate.
Trust: Given a long meeting is processed, When I review the audit logs, Then the processing should be logged with timestamps.
Given the system is set up for the first time, When a meeting is detected, Then the detection process should be idempotent and logged in the audit trail.
Given the system has already detected a meeting, When the detection process is triggered again, Then no duplicate entries should be created in the audit trail.
Trust: Given any detection process, When it completes, Then an entry is created in the audit trail with a timestamp and status.
Given a non-technical user, When accessing the system, Then the interface should present simple options by default.
Given an experienced user, When accessing advanced settings, Then additional configuration options should be available.
Trust: Given any user action, When a setting is changed, Then the change is logged with user details in the audit trail.
Given the demo, when demo/index.html is opened, then every screen in its navigation is reachable and every record opens one level down.
Given any demo screen, when it is shown, then a permanent banner says the data is sample data and names the plan version the demo was built from.
Given the demo, when any screen renders, then demo/demo-spec.json is committed in this repo and every screen, row and count comes from that file rather than from values typed into the page.

Given .colaberry/plan.json, when the demo is built, then every story with a workspace has a screen or a stated reason for having none, and every agent and every guardrail in the plan appears in the demo.
Given the Command Center, when it is opened, then it links to the demo and shows none of the demo's sample values as its own.
Trust — no sample row breaks a guardrail in the plan, and no restricted field holds a value.
